references.text: Here the commandment of circumcision on the eighth day is established, even if it falls on a Sabbath, which sets forth the halakhic principle Jesus refers to: that the law of circumcision overrides the Sabbath prohibition.

Jesus asks a similar question about whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath, using the example of a sheep falling into a pit to justify healing, paralleling the argument about circumcision in John 7:23.

Jesus criticizes the Pharisees for breaking God's commandments to uphold human traditions, just as in John 7:23 he accuses them of violating the spirit of the law (healing) while clinging to its letter (Sabbath observance), even though they themselves break the law by performing circumcision on the Sabbath.

Jesus heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath and asks whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath, reflecting the logic in John 7:23 where healing an entire person is compared to circumcising one limb.
